name: Sir Henry Taylor
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Sir Henry Taylor (1800–1886) was an English dramatist and poet who also served as an official in the Colonial Office; his best-known work is the verse drama Philip van Artevelde.
The poems here are taken from Arthur Quiller-Couch's anthology The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (Clarendon Press, 1912).

poems.title: Elena's Song
poems.author: Sir Henry Taylor
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
Quoth tongue of neither maid nor wife
To heart of neither wife nor maid —
Lead we not here a jolly life
Betwixt the shine and shade?
Quoth

Quoth heart of neither maid nor wife
To tongue of neither wife nor maid —
Thou wagg'st, but I am worn with strife,
And feel like flowers that fade.

poems.title: Song
poems.author: Sir Henry Taylor
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
The bee to the heather,
The lark to the sky,
The roe to the greenwood,
And whither shall I?

O, Alice! Ah, Alice!
So sweet to the bee
Are the moorland and heather
By Cannock and Leigh!

O, Alice! Ah, Alice!
O'er Teddesley Park
The sunny sky scatters
The notes of the lark!

O, Alice! Ah, Alice!
In Beaudesert glade
The roes toss their antlers
For joy of the shade! —

But Alice, dear Alice!
Glade, moorland, nor sky
Without you can content me —
And whither shall I?

poems.title: Women Singing
poems.author: Sir Henry Taylor
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
By Wellesbourne and Charlcote ford,
At break of day, I saw a sword.
Wessex warriors, rank by rank,
Rose on Avon's hither bank;
Mercia's men in fair array
Look'd at them from Marraway;
Close and closer ranged they soon,
And the battle join'd at noon.

By Wellesbourne and Charlcote Lea
I heard a sound as of the sea:
Thirty thousand rushing men,
Twenty thousand met by ten;
Rang the shield and brake the shaft,
Tosty yell'd, Harcather laugh'd;
Thoro' Avon's waters red
Chased by ten the twenty fled.

By Charlcote ford and Wellesbourne
I saw the moon's pale face forlorn.
River flow'd and rushes sigh'd,
Wounded warriors groan'd and died;
Ella took his early rest,
The raven stood on his white breast;
Hoarsely in the dead man's ear
Raven whisper'd, 'Friend, good cheer!
Ere the winter pinch the crow
He that slew thee shall lie low.'

Heida sings:

Love ye wisely, love ye well;
Challenge then the gates of Hell!
Love and Truth can ride it out,
Come bridal song or battle shout.
